chunks.text: 31-year-old female, Professional, resident of Choa Chu Kang, Singapore.
History of pneumonia resolved 5 years ago
Remote history of left wrist fracture (healed)
Previous use of Omeprazole for GERD, discontinued 2 years ago

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms. [Patient's Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go over a few things to make sure everything goes smoothly for you. Can you please tell me a bit about why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doctor. I've been having a lot of pain in my tummy, especially after eating. The doctor said it's because of gallstones, so they're removing my gallbladder laparoscopically.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. And how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: About six months now, on and off. It got worse last week, so they decided to take it out.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, let's go over your medical history. You have a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and obesity. Are all these conditions well under control?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, lah. My sugar levels are okay with the metformin, blood pressure is stable with lisinopril, and I'm trying to eat better and walk more.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great to hear that. Now, let's talk about your medications. You're currently on metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg once daily, atorvastatin 20 mg once daily, and you've stopped ranitidine. Is that correct?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, that's right. I stopped the ranitidine as advised.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Now, regarding allergies, the records say 'no known allergies', but I understand there might be something more to add here. Can you confirm if you have any allergies to antibiotics, including cephalosporins, in addition to penicillin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, right. I forgot to mention that. I had a reaction to a cephalosporin antibiotic once — I think it was ceftriaxone — and I had nausea and vomiting. Not as bad as the penicillin rash, but still a reaction.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for letting me know. That's very important. We'll make sure to avoid cephalosporins during your care. Are you currently on any other medications or supplements, including traditional or herbal remedies?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, just the ones I mentioned. No herbs or anything like that.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, did you have any issues with it?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had a minor procedure a few years back, a colonoscopy, and I was under sedation. I woke up fine, no problems.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. And how are you with your mobility and daily activities? Can you walk up a flight of stairs without difficulty?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I can still walk and do most things, though I do get a bit tired sometimes. But I can manage my daily activities.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Lastly, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I've been fasting as instructed. Just a sip of water with my morning meds, but that was hours ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. We'll be using general anesthesia for your surgery, and we'll also be using intraoperative neuromonitoring as part of the procedure. If you have any questions or concerns, feel free to ask.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No questions, doctor. I think that's all covered.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] lactated ringers one thousand milliliters given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, I guess. Still a bit groggy, but I can talk.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Can you tell me your pain level out of 10? Any discomfort at the incision sites or elsewhere?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: It's about a 4 or 5. There's some soreness in the tummy area, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks. Have you felt nauseous at all since waking up? Any vomiting or dizziness?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, no nausea. I feel a bit thirsty, but nothing else.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. How's your breathing? Any shortness of breath or discomfort when taking deep breaths?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine. I can take deep breaths without pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Did you experience any awareness or discomfort during the surgery that you'd like to share?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don’t remember anything. I was out the whole time.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Lastly, with your diabetes and high blood pressure, have you noticed any unusual symptoms like dizziness, chest pain, or vision changes?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing like that. I feel stable, just tired.
